title: Heuristic-driven comm/compute kernel affinity and KV-window overlap for TP runtime
author: Arjun Patel
release_notes: Introduce a heuristic kernel affinity scheduler and KV-windowed prefetch to improve overlap between NCCL collectives and compute for tensor-parallel workloads. Default disabled behind tp_affinity_v2 feature flag. Expected improvement: p95 latency -12%, throughput +9% on 8xA100 for seq=1024 workloads.
description:
Motivation: On multi-GPU tensor-parallel (TP) workloads we observed periodic stalls and poor tail latency due to inefficient interleaving of collective operations (NCCL) and compute kernels. The runtime was launching kernels with a naive round-robin stream assignment which caused kernel/comm contention, suboptimal kernel placement, and missed opportunities to prefetch KV cache entries in time for subsequent microbatches. This PR introduces a heuristic-driven kernel affinity scheduler and a small KV-window prefetcher that together increase overlap between comm and compute and reduce context-switch overheads.

What this PR changes: 1) A lightweight affinity heuristic (runtime/scheduler/affinity_scheduler.cpp) that classifies kernels by predicted device memory working set, comm participation (collective vs local), and expected duration. Affinity rules prefer assigning high-comm kernels to isolated comm streams while GPU-heavy compute kernels land on compute-optimized streams. 2) Kernel bundling: adjacent small kernels are grouped to reduce kernel launch overhead for short-lived ops. 3) KV-windowed prefetcher (kvcache/prefetcher.cpp) which issues early KV prefetches for the next N microbatches when the affinity heuristic predicts a contended comm phase. The window size is tunable per deployment and conservatively defaults to 2 microbatches. 4) NCCL adapter updates to annotate collective launches with affinity hints and to expose a lightweight async progress hint for host-side pacing (nccl/adapter.cpp). 5) New telemetry and histograms (observability/tp_affinity_metrics.*) to track comm/compute overlap, kernel stream distribution, and KV-prefetch hit rate. 6) Feature flag tp_affinity_v2 (config/feature_flags.yaml) - opt-in by default for safety.

Benchmarks: Microbenchmarks run on 8xA100, sequence length 1024, synthetic batching with mixed prompt lengths. Results: p50 ~ +3% throughput, p95 latency -12%, overall token/sec +9% for typical real-world mixes (documented in tests/integration/tp_affinity_bench.py). Gains are most pronounced at p95 and under mixed-size request distributions.

Compatibility and safety: The scheduler is conservative by default and the feature is gated behind tp_affinity_v2. When disabled behavior is identical to baseline. The KV-window prefetcher includes memory safety checks and refuses to expand the window if device memory headroom is below a configured threshold.

Testing and CI: Added unit tests for the affinity rules and prefetch heuristics (tests/unit/test_affinity_scheduler.cpp, tests/unit/test_kv_prefetcher.cpp) and an integration benchmark used in perf CI (tests/integration/tp_affinity_bench.py). CI initially flagged a flaky allreduce deadlock during the first integration run; root cause was a missing barrier in the nccl adapter when a prefetch completed concurrently with stream reordering. Extra synchronization and a retry path were added to fix the flake.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-1824) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration perf bench - [x] Feature flag and safe defaults - [x] Observability metrics - [x] Release notes entry

Notes: This change touches the kernel scheduler and NCCL integration path; recommend a staged rollout with canary on Dedicated before enabling broadly. The heuristics are intentionally lightweight; future follow-ups can add topology-aware optimizations and ML-driven affinity estimation.

review_comments: Maya Chen: Please add accounting for transient device allocations in the affinity heuristic; without that we risk overcommitting when kernels allocate temporary buffers. Also add unit test that simulates a small headroom scenario.
Arjun Patel (author): Added transient alloc tracking and a unit test that triggers the memory-guard behavior when headroom < 10%. See tests/unit/test_kv_prefetcher.cpp commit c54d21f.
Lena Torres: Strong preference to keep the feature off by default in hosted for at least one release cycle. Please ensure the flag default is false and document rollback steps.
Arjun Patel (author): Confirmed tp_affinity_v2 defaults to false in config/feature_flags.yaml and added a rollback paragraph to docs/release_notes/tp_affinity_v2.md.
Omar Haddad: How does this behave on heterogeneous topologies (NVLink vs PCIe)? We should avoid worse-than-baseline cases. Consider falling back to baseline when detected cross-node bandwidth is low.

Arjun Patel (author): Added topology-weighted affinity multiplier and a safe fallback to baseline when measured link bandwidth between peers falls below configured threshold. See affinity_scheduler.cpp update.
Maya Chen: CI integration bench flagged an allreduce hang on first run, please describe the mitigation.

Arjun Patel (author): Root cause was a race between host-side prefetch callback and stream reorder; added a lightweight barrier in nccl adapter and a retry path for in-flight collectives. Covered by integration test enhancements.
merge_summary: Merged by Maya Chen via squash merge. Squash commit message: 'tp: heuristic-driven comm/compute kernel affinity + KV-window prefetch (ENG-1824)'. Deploy gated behind tp_affinity_v2=false by default; follow rollout plan in docs/release_notes/tp_affinity_v2.md.
notes: Follow-ups: 1) topology-aware cost model (ENG-1902) 2) automatic window tuning via light-weight sampling 3) extended metrics for per-model affinity auditing. Recommended canary on Dedicated for 48h before enabling hosted customers.
